key_insight: In aligned MAPbI3 nanowalls, ferroelastic symmetry breaking does more than broaden excitons—it splits them into polarization-selective states and introduces lattice-coupled excitations across the phase transition.
engineering_relevance: This suggests perovskite optoelectronic performance can be tuned by controlling crystal texture, symmetry, and phase coexistence to achieve anisotropic and switchable optical responses.
evidence_signal: At 5 K the orthorhombic phase shows a 45 meV polarization-selective excitonic splitting, and near 160 K a lower-energy lattice-coupled state appears 58 meV below the split excitonic feature.
watch_item: The effects are demonstrated in highly aligned nanowalls with a well-defined optical axis, so translating the behavior to less ordered films or devices may require careful texture control.
paper_title: Ferroelastic exciton splitting in hybrid perovskite nanowalls
